correctness.rationale: Each one with z preceding zeros contributes z(a−z); summing by consecutive one-runs gives a weighted sum on distinct productive cuts. Fixed orientation has t productive one-runs and u unproductive boundary runs. Since positive run lengths cost t+u ones, all extras must be allocated to productive highest-weight cuts, and strict concavity maximizes the selected weights at t cuts nearest a/2. The sorted losses 0,1,1,4,4,… (even a) or 0,0,2,2,6,6,… (odd a) sum to the displayed cubic Δ_a(t). Enumerating zero-ended and one-ended orientations gives the formulas and exact equality counts Q, including R=2 and (a,R)=(1,3). Independently enumerated all words with lengths 2..13, comparing 400 composition/run maxima and multiplicities. This checks finite cases only.

value.rationale: Fixing both Parikh counts and the exact number of symbol-runs introduces a genuine fragmentation penalty absent from unrestricted subsequence bounds. The theorem is a complete infinite three-parameter extremal answer for the simplest scattered alternating triple, giving sharp cubic parity law, all witnesses and their multiplicities; the central-cut optimization is reusable for constrained word statistics. It is not a claim for general patterns.
